pll1d15c5-d1e3477.summary: Objection: if the Son was sent by himself, why does he say 'I have not come of myself' (John 7:28; 8:42)?

pll1d15c5-d1e3491.summary: Answers with De Trinitate II: this is said according to the form of a servant, in which he did not bring about his sending or work the incarnation, but he did so according to the form of God.
claims: The text refers to Christ's humanity.
According to his divinity the Son worked the incarnation.

pl-l1d15c5.summary: Answers the objection from John 7:28 / 8:42, 'I have not come of myself': with Augustine, this is said according to the form of a servant, in which he did not bring about his own sending, that is, did not work the incarnation; according to the form of God he did.
claims: 'I have not come of myself' is said according to the form of a servant.
As man, the Son did not effect the incarnation; as God he did.
